title: Responsive design
summary: Make a layout adapt to the screen with the viewport meta tag and media queries.

quiz.q: Why does a mobile-friendly page need `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">`?
options: It adds a border to the screen
Without it, phones pretend to be about 980px wide and shrink the page
quiz.explain: Without the tag, mobile browsers lay the page out on a wide virtual screen and zoom out. The tag asks for the real device width.

options: Only when the window is exactly 600px
When the window is 600px wide or wider
When the window is 600px wide or narrower
quiz.explain: `min-width` means this width and up. `max-width: 600px` means this width and down.

quiz.q: The window is 800px wide. What is the final `flex-direction`?
quiz.explain: 800px is at least 600px, so the media rule applies. It comes later, so it overrides the base rule.

quiz.q: Write the media query that targets screens at most 500px wide.
quiz.explain: `max-width` is the upper limit. Phones usually fall in this range.

options: Writes the small-screen styles as the base, then adds min-width queries for larger screens
quiz.explain: Mobile-first starts simple and layers on complexity as space allows. It keeps the base CSS small.

exercise.task:
Make the layout responsive. The frame is 800px wide, so wide-screen rules apply. Work in `index.html`.

- Add `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">` inside `<head>`.
- `.layout` is a flex container that stacks in a column by default (already written).
- Add `@media (min-width: 600px)` that sets `.layout` to `flex-direction: row`.
- Add `@media (max-width: 500px)` that hides `.sidebar` with `display: none`.
hints: Media queries wrap normal rules: `@media (condition) { selector { ... } }`.
min-width applies when the window is at least that wide. At 800px the min-width rule is active but the max-width rule is not.

<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">

@media (min-width: 600px) {
  .layout {
    flex-direction: row;
  }
}
@media (max-width: 500px) {
  .sidebar {
    display: none;
  }
}

checks.name: The viewport meta tag is present
checks.hint: Add the viewport meta tag inside head.

checks.name: At 800px wide, .layout is a row
checks.hint: Inside the min-width: 600px query set .layout { flex-direction: row; }.

checks.name: At 800px wide, the sidebar is still visible
checks.hint: The sidebar should be hidden only inside the max-width: 500px query.

checks.name: The max-width query hides the sidebar
checks.hint: Inside the max-width: 500px query add .sidebar { display: none; }.
